headline: The iPhone reached shops in June, the Dow passed 14,000 in July, and Benazir Bhutto was killed in December
texture: Tumblr opened to the public on February 19. Justin.tv launched as a site for streaming video games. Rupert Murdoch bought Dow Jones and Company, and with it the Wall Street Journal, for $5 billion. WikiLeaks published the standard US army protocol for Guantanamo Bay on November 7. Comet McNaught came close enough in January to be seen in daylight, and astronomers found Gliese 581c in the constellation Libra in April.

Gross world product grew 3.7 percent, down from 3.9 the year before, and inflation in the developed economies ran at 1.9 percent. Oil prices climbed as demand from developing countries outran spare capacity, and biofuel production pushed up the price of wheat and maize. Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum gave 7.41 billion euros to an education foundation on May 20. Iraq ended the year as the source of 2.3 million refugees, behind Afghanistan's 3.1 million.

Spider-Man 3 took $151,116,516 over one weekend in May, past the record held by Pirates of the Caribbean: Dead Man's Chest. High School Musical 2 drew 17.24 million viewers to the Disney Channel on August 17, and ESPN's Monday Night Football beat that basic cable record on December 3 with 17.52 million watching the unbeaten Patriots. Bob Barker hosted The Price Is Right for the last time on June 15 after 35 years, and Drew Carey took the job on October 15. George Mitchell named 89 baseball players as steroid users on December 13.

pol.us_president.label: US President
pol.us_president.detail: Seventh year of his presidency, with Dick Cheney as vice president and John Roberts as chief justice.

pol.us_congress.label: US Congress
pol.us_congress.value: 110th Congress from January 3, with Nancy Pelosi the first woman to hold the speakership
pol.us_congress.detail: Pelosi took the chair on January 4, succeeding Dennis Hastert. Harry Reid replaced Bill Frist as Senate majority leader.

pol.iraq_surge.label: Iraq troop surge
pol.iraq_surge.value: Bush announced an increase in US troops in Iraq in an address to the nation
pol.iraq_surge.detail: The US page dates the beginning of the surge to the same day the announcement was made.

pol.virginia_tech.label: Virginia Tech shooting
pol.virginia_tech.value: Seung-Hui Cho, aged 23, shot 32 people dead and injured 17 others before killing himself as police reached the scene

pol.obama_candidacy.label: Obama declares
pol.obama_candidacy.value: Senator Barack Obama of Illinois announced he would run for president

pol.bridge_collapse.label: I-35W bridge collapse
pol.bridge_collapse.value: The Interstate 35W bridge over the Mississippi River in Minneapolis fell at 6:05 in the evening, killing 13 people
pol.bridge_collapse.detail: It came down during the later part of rush hour, between University Avenue and Washington Avenue.

pol.subprime_crisis.label: Subprime mortgage crisis
pol.subprime_crisis.value: BNP Paribas blocked withdrawals from three hedge funds heavily committed in subprime lending
pol.subprime_crisis.detail: American housing prices fell in the later part of the year.

world.uk_pm.label: UK Prime Minister
world.uk_pm.value: Tony Blair until June 27, then Gordon Brown (Labour)
world.uk_pm.detail: Blair announced on May 10 that he would give up the Labour leadership and the office. Brown ran unopposed in the leadership election and promised political continuity.

world.france_president.label: President of France
world.france_president.value: Nicolas Sarkozy, elected in the second round on May 6
world.france_president.detail: He pursued several changes, among them a push to lengthen the 35 hour working week.

world.eu_enlargement.label: EU takes two new members
world.eu_enlargement.value: Bulgaria and Romania joined the European Union, and Slovenia adopted the euro the same day
world.eu_enlargement.detail: On December 21 the Czech Republic, Estonia, Hungary, Latvia, Lithuania, Malta, Poland, Slovakia and Slovenia joined the Schengen border-free zone.

world.bhutto.label: Benazir Bhutto assassinated
world.bhutto.value: The former prime minister of Pakistan was killed with 20 other people at an election rally in Rawalpindi
world.bhutto.detail: Pervez Musharraf had given up his military position and then ruled under a state of emergency earlier in the year.

world.gaza.label: Battle of Gaza
world.gaza.value: Hamas defeated Palestinian Authority forces and took control of the Gaza Strip
world.gaza.detail: Fought June 10 to 15. Palestine ended the year with two governments, Hamas in Gaza and Fatah in the West Bank.

world.ipcc.label: IPCC fourth assessment report
world.ipcc.value: The panel concluded that climate change is very likely to have a predominantly human cause
world.ipcc.detail: Published February 2. The Arctic ice pack melted at ten times the annual average, and the Northwest Passage was clear of ice through the summer for the first time.

film.gross.label: Highest-grossing films, worldwide
value: Pirates of the Caribbean: At World's End, $963,400,492, Disney
Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix, $941,676,843, Warner Bros.
film.gross.detail: Worldwide gross, which is the basis the source ranks by. Ratatouille came sixth, I Am Legend seventh and The Simpsons Movie eighth.

film.best_picture.label: Best Picture
film.best_picture.detail: Awarded at the 80th Academy Awards the following February. It won four awards, and Joel and Ethan Coen became the second pair of directors to take Best Director for the same film. It tied There Will Be Blood for most nominations with eight.

film.acting_awards.label: Acting awards
value: Best Actor: Daniel Day-Lewis, There Will Be Blood
Best Actress: Marion Cotillard, La Vie en Rose
Best Supporting Actor: Javier Bardem, No Country for Old Men
Best Supporting Actress: Tilda Swinton, Michael Clayton
film.acting_awards.detail: None of the four winners was American, which had happened only once before. Cotillard was the first person to win Best Actress for a French-language performance.

film.world_cinema.label: Nominated for Best Foreign Language Film

film.how_people_watched.label: How people watched
film.how_people_watched.value: In a theatre, then on DVD, and for the first time over the internet to a personal computer
film.how_people_watched.detail: Netflix began delivering films to subscribers' computers in January, and Hulu opened in October.

tv.top_shows.label: Most-watched programs, season starting autumn 2007
value: Dancing with the Stars, Monday, ABC, 14.0
Dancing with the Stars, Wednesday, ABC, 12.6
tv.top_shows.detail: Nielsen reports by season rather than calendar year, so this covers the season that began in autumn and ran to the following spring. The Writers Guild strike from November 5 cut into it.

tv.premieres.label: New series
value: The Big Bang Theory, CBS, September 24

tv.sopranos_finale.label: The Sopranos ended
tv.sopranos_finale.value: The last episode, Made in America, closed with a cut to black
tv.sopranos_finale.detail: The series had run on HBO since 1999.

tv.writers_strike.label: Writers Guild strike
tv.writers_strike.value: 12,000 Writers Guild of America members walked out against film and television studios
tv.writers_strike.detail: Production on television shows stopped and network schedules were badly disrupted.

music.hot100_year_end.label: Year-end Hot 100 number one
music.hot100_year_end.detail: Umbrella by Rihanna featuring Jay-Z came second and The Sweet Escape by Gwen Stefani featuring Akon third. Justin Timberlake had seven songs on the chart, more than anyone else.

music.listening_format.label: How people listened
music.listening_format.value: Radiohead released In Rainbows as a download that buyers priced themselves, ten days after announcing it
music.listening_format.detail: Jonny Greenwood posted the announcement on the band's website on October 1.

music.best_selling_album.label: Best-selling album in the US
music.best_selling_album.detail: Billboard's top seller of the year, ahead of Konvicted by Akon and The Dutchess by Fergie. The two cached pages disagree about the global number one: the year article names the High School Musical 2 soundtrack and the music article's IFPI table names The Best Damn Thing by Avril Lavigne, both citing the same IFPI list.

music.grammys.label: 49th Grammy Awards
music.grammys.value: The Dixie Chicks took five awards with producer Rick Rubin, including Record, Album and Song of the Year
music.grammys.detail: Held at the Staples Center in Los Angeles. Carrie Underwood won Best New Artist, and the Police reunited to open the show, their first performance of the century.

music.eurovision.label: Eurovision Song Contest
music.eurovision.value: Marija Šerifović won for Serbia with Molitva
music.eurovision.detail: Held in Helsinki from May 10 to 12.

tech.iphone.label: iPhone
tech.iphone.value: Steve Jobs introduced it at a Macworld keynote in San Francisco on January 9, and it went on sale in the United States on June 29
tech.iphone.detail: Queues formed around Apple Stores at release. It reached the United Kingdom, Ireland, France, Germany and Austria in November.

tech.online_streaming.label: Netflix and Hulu start streaming
tech.online_streaming.value: Netflix began delivering films over the internet on January 16, and Hulu opened on October 29
tech.online_streaming.detail: Both are listed among the year's new over-the-top services.

tech.games.label: Games
value: Call of Duty 4: Modern Warfare, November 5
Mass Effect and Rock Band, November 20
tech.games.detail: Super Mario Galaxy was the year's most critically acclaimed title. Assassin's Creed, Crysis, Portal, Skate, The Witcher and Uncharted were also new properties.

tech.game_sales.label: Best sellers in the US
tech.game_sales.value: Halo 3 sold 4.82 million copies, ahead of Wii Play at 4.12 million and Call of Duty 4 at 3.04 million
tech.game_sales.detail: NPD figures. The Nintendo DS was the year's best-selling console, at 8,500,000 units in North America and 24,343,702 across Japan, North America and Europe.

tech.android.label: Android
tech.android.value: The Open Handset Alliance launched the Android mobile operating system

tech.social_hashtag.label: The hashtag
tech.social_hashtag.value: Chris Messina proposed using the pound sign to mark groups on Twitter

tech.windows_vista.label: Windows Vista
tech.windows_vista.value: Microsoft released it to consumers on January 30, alongside Office 2007

prices.gas.label: Average US gas price
prices.gas.detail: Unleaded regular, US city average, including taxes, annual average.

prices.min_wage.label: Federal minimum wage
prices.min_wage.detail: The basic rate for covered nonfarm workers, as in effect on December 31.

prices.dow.label: Dow Jones Industrial Average
prices.dow.value: Closed above 13,000 for the first time on April 25, and above 14,000 on July 19
prices.dow.detail: It reached an all-time high of 14,164 on October 9 and then began to fall. Its worst single day of the year was a loss of 387.18 points on August 9.

culture.mood.label: Mood
culture.mood.value: Queues outside phone shops, a Nobel Peace Prize shared between a former vice president and a climate panel, and hedge funds shutting their doors in August.

culture.nobel_prizes.label: Nobel Prizes
value: Peace: Al Gore and the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change
Physics: Albert Fert and Peter Grünberg
Physiology or Medicine: Mario Capecchi, Oliver Smithies and Martin Evans
Economics: Leonid Hurwicz, Eric Maskin and Roger Myerson

sports.super_bowl.label: Super Bowl XLI
sports.super_bowl.detail: Played at Dolphin Stadium in Miami Gardens. The Colts' second title, and their first since the franchise left Baltimore.

sports.world_series.label: World Series
sports.world_series.value: Boston Red Sox swept the Colorado Rockies in four games

sports.nba_finals.label: NBA Finals
sports.nba_finals.value: San Antonio Spurs swept the Cleveland Cavaliers in four games for their fourth title
sports.nba_finals.detail: Tony Parker was named Finals most valuable player.

sports.stanley_cup.label: Stanley Cup
sports.stanley_cup.value: Anaheim Ducks beat the Ottawa Senators in five games
sports.stanley_cup.detail: Scott Niedermayer of the Ducks won the Conn Smythe Trophy as playoff most valuable player.

sports.home_run_record.label: Career home run record
sports.home_run_record.value: Barry Bonds hit his 756th, passing Hank Aaron's mark of 755
sports.home_run_record.detail: Struck amid questions about his suspected use of performance-enhancing drugs.

sports.rugby_world_cup.label: Rugby World Cup
sports.rugby_world_cup.value: South Africa beat the defending champions England 15 to 6 in the final
sports.rugby_world_cup.detail: Played in France from September 7 to October 20, with matches also in Edinburgh and Cardiff.

deaths.johnson.label: Lady Bird Johnson
deaths.johnson.detail: First Lady of the United States as the wife of Lyndon B. Johnson.

notes: Research pass July 2026. Box office is worldwide gross: the film page's table column reads "Worldwide gross" and the sentence above it says the top 10 films released in 2007 by worldwide gross, so the territory is named in both the label and the detail. The 80th Academy Awards ceremony fell in February of the following year, which is why film.best_picture says "the following February" instead of the date. Nielsen figures are for the season that started in autumn and ran to the following spring, labelled that way, and the Writers Guild walkout from November 5 shortened it. The two cached pages disagree about the year's best-selling album worldwide, both citing the same IFPI list: the year article names the High School Musical 2 soundtrack while the music article's table names The Best Damn Thing by Avril Lavigne. Rather than pick, the file states only the Billboard top seller in the US and names the disagreement in the fact detail. Dropped for want of a source that carried the whole claim: attendance at Super Bowl XLI, which sits on the sports page while the date, score and venue sit on the US page; Alberto Contador's Tour de France win, which the sports page gives with no date; and the US page's December line that the recession began with unemployment at 5 percent, which the page itself flags as needing a citation. Left out over the anachronism rule and not explained on the page: the International Olympic Committee awarding Sochi the Winter Games on July 4, and the cancelled Armenia against Azerbaijan European Championship qualifiers of August 10, both of which name a year more than one out from this one and so need allowlist entries.
